title: Past Perfect & Future Perfect
description: Learn the past perfect (had + V3) and future perfect (will have + V3) for Grade 7: form, uses, sequence of events and signal words — with bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Past Perfect Tense
topics.concept:
The past perfect shows that one past action happened before another past action. Form: had + past participle (V3) — the same for all subjects.

  • The film had started when we arrived. (starting came first)
  • By the time he came, she had left.

The earlier action takes the past perfect; the later action takes the simple past.

Signal words: before, after, by the time, already, just, when, until then.

examples.problem: Complete: When I reached home, my mother ___ (cook) dinner.
examples.solution: had cooked — the cooking finished before I reached home, so use the past perfect.

examples.problem: Which action is earlier: The bell had rung before the teacher came.?
examples.solution: The bell ringing — it is in the past perfect ('had rung'), so it happened first.

recap: Past perfect = had + V3, for the earlier of two past actions
The later action takes the simple past
Signal words: before, after, by the time, already, when

topics.title: Future Perfect Tense
topics.concept:
The future perfect describes an action that will be completed before a stated future time. Form: will have + past participle (V3).

  • By 2030, scientists will have found a cure.
  • By next month, she will have saved enough money.
  • I will have finished my homework by 8 p.m.

It almost always appears with a 'by + future time' phrase that marks the deadline.

Signal words: by, by then, by the time, before, in two years.

examples.solution: will have completed — the action finishes before Friday.

examples.problem: Why use the future perfect here: By the time you wake up, I will have left.?
examples.solution: Leaving will be finished before the future moment 'you wake up', so the future perfect is right.

recap: Shows an action finished before a future time
Usually with 'by + future time' (by 2030, by then)

questions.q: 'The plane ___ before we reached the airport.'
questions.explanation: Earlier past action → 'had left'.

questions.q: Future perfect of 'complete':
questions.explanation: will have + V3.

questions.q: Past participle after 'had': 'She had ___ the book.'
questions.explanation: 'read' (V3) follows 'had'.

questions.q: 'By Sunday they ___ painting the house.'
questions.explanation: Future deadline → future perfect.

questions.q: Which is the earlier action? 'After the guests had gone, we slept.'
questions.explanation: 'had gone' is the earlier past action.

questions.q: 'He ___ his keys before he reached the door.'
questions.explanation: Earlier action → past perfect 'had lost'.

questions.q: Signal word for the past perfect:
questions.explanation: 'by the time' (with a past clause) → past perfect.

questions.q: 'By 10 o'clock, I ___ my dinner.'
questions.explanation: Finished before a future time → future perfect.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: had + written (V3).

questions.q: 'They ___ already left when we phoned.'
questions.explanation: Past context → 'had already left'.

questions.q: 'By the time you arrive, the meeting ___.'
questions.explanation: Finished before a future point → future perfect.

questions.q: Which uses the simple past correctly (not past perfect)?
questions.explanation: A single past action with a clear time → simple past 'went'.

questions.q: Spot the error: 'No sooner had the bell rung than the students have left.'
questions.explanation: Both clauses are past; the later needs the past tense: 'than the students left' (or 'had left' is replaced by simple past). Standard form: 'No sooner had the bell rung than the students left.'

questions.q: Choose the correct option: 'By the time the doctor ___, the patient ___ already recovered.'
questions.explanation: Later action = simple past 'came'; earlier = past perfect 'had recovered'.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'Hardly had I sat down when the phone has rung.'
questions.explanation: After 'Hardly had …', the second clause takes the simple past: 'when the phone rang'.

questions.q: Fill in: 'By 2040, renewable energy ___ most fossil fuels.'
questions.explanation: Completed before a future time → future perfect.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: She said she had saw the film.
She said she had seen the film.
She said she has seen the film yesterday.
She said she had see the film.
questions.explanation: Past perfect needs the participle 'seen' after 'had'.

questions.q: Choose: 'Scarcely had the train started ___ it stopped again.'
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely … when' is the correct pairing.

questions.q: Rearrange: 'finished / by / will / noon / I / have / it'
options: By noon I will have finished it.
I will by noon have finished it.
By noon will I have finished it.
I have finished it will by noon.
questions.explanation: 'By noon I will have finished it.' is correct.

questions.q: Choose the right sequence: 'The thief ___ before the police ___.'
questions.explanation: Earlier = past perfect 'had escaped'; later = simple past 'arrived'.

outcomes: Form the past perfect (had + V3) and future perfect (will have + V3)
Use the past perfect for the earlier of two past actions
Use the future perfect for an action finished by a future time
Apply signal words like by the time, before, after, by 2030
Avoid mixing up the past simple and the past perfect

intro.en: The past perfect is the 'past before the past'. When two things happened in the past, the one that happened first takes had + V3. The future perfect looks ahead: it describes an action that will be finished before a certain future time, using will have + V3.
intro.hi: Past Perfect 'भूत से भी पहले का भूत' है। जब भूतकाल में दो घटनाएँ हों, तो जो पहले हुई वह had + V3 लेती है। Future Perfect आगे देखता है: यह ऐसी क्रिया बताता है जो किसी भविष्य-समय से पहले पूरी हो चुकी होगी, रूप will have + V3।

real_life.situation:
You explain why you missed a friend:

You: By the time I reached the station, the train had already left. Don't worry — by tonight I will have booked another ticket.
real_life.why: 'had left' happened before 'I reached' (past perfect for the earlier action); 'will have booked' will be complete before tonight (future perfect). Both tenses fix the order of events in time.

rule_box.html:
TenseFormExample
Past PerfectS + had + V3She had finished.
Future PerfectS + will have + V3She will have finished.
rule_box.formula: Past Perfect = had + V3 · Future Perfect = will have + V3
rule_box.example: He had eaten before I came. By 9, he will have eaten.

quick_test.q: The past perfect is used for the action that happened:
quick_test.explanation: The past perfect marks the earlier of two past actions (had + V3).

common_mistakes.wrong: When I arrived, the train left already.
common_mistakes.right: When I arrived, the train had already left.
common_mistakes.note: The earlier action needs the past perfect 'had left'.

common_mistakes.right: By 2030 they will have found a cure.

common_mistakes.note: A single past action with a clear time needs the simple past.

error_detection.correct: By 2025 they will have found the cure.

sentence_correction.correct: The match had started before we reached.

rearrangement.jumbled: had / before / she / gone / I / arrived
rearrangement.answer: She had gone before I arrived.

answers: before / by the time → past perfect signal

reading.passage: By the time the firefighters arrived, the small shop had already burned down. The owner had locked up at nine, long before the fire started. "By tomorrow," the officer said, "we will have completed our investigation, and by next month the family will have rebuilt the shop."

questions.q: Which action happened first — the fire or the firefighters arriving?
questions.answer: The shop burning down happened first (past perfect 'had burned'), before the firefighters arrived.

questions.q: Find a future perfect verb in the passage.
questions.answer: will have completed (also 'will have rebuilt') — an action finished before a future time.

questions.q: Why is 'had locked' in the past perfect?
questions.answer: Locking up at nine happened before the fire — the earlier past action.

speaking: The train had left before I reached the platform.
She had finished her homework by the time dinner was ready.
By next year, I will have learned to drive.
They had already eaten when the guests came.
By 9 p.m., we will have completed the project.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences about events in order, using the past perfect for the earlier action and the future perfect for a future deadline.
writing.example: By the time the bell rang, I had packed my bag. By tomorrow I will have submitted the form.

micro_quiz.explanation: The earlier past action → past perfect 'had started'.

micro_quiz.q: Choose: 'She had ___ the door before leaving.'
Which signal goes with the future perfect?
micro_quiz.explanation: 'by next week' marks a future deadline → future perfect.

options: After she had finished, she will rest.
After she had finished, she rested.
After she finished, she had rested.
After she has finished, she rested.
challenge.explanation: Earlier action = past perfect 'had finished'; later = simple past 'rested'.

challenge.q: Identify the error: 'By the time the rescue team will arrive, the flood will have receded.'
challenge.explanation: In a time clause, use the simple present: 'By the time the rescue team arrives …'.

challenge.q: Which sentence correctly uses the past perfect?
options: I had never seen such a sight before that day.
challenge.explanation: Past perfect needs a reference to an earlier point ('before that day') and the participle 'seen'.
